 WASHINGTON (7News) — Move your car before heading to bed Saturday if it is parked along the Marine Corps Marathon route. Emergency no-parking restrictions begin at 2 a.m. Sunday in parts of D.C., followed by widespread street and bridge closures ahead of the race.
 The 51st Marine Corps Marathon takes place Sunday, Oct. 25, with the main race starting at 7:20 a.m. on Route 110 in Arlington . Drivers should plan alternate routes through Georgetown, the National Mall, Rosslyn, the Pentagon area and Crystal City.
 RELATED | Marine Corps Marathon weather: From the coldest start to the wettest race 
 Restrictions on part of southbound Route 110 were scheduled to begin at 4 p.m. Saturday. More Arlington closures begin around 3 a.m. Sunday, with some continuing until approximately 6 p.m.
 D.C. parking restrictions begin at 2 a.m. 
 Emergency no-parking restrictions are scheduled from 2 a.m. to 2 p.m. Sunday along these streets:
 Third, Seventh and 14th streets between Constitution Avenue NW and Independence Avenue SW.
 M Street NW between Canal Road and Wisconsin Avenue.
 Canal Road NW between Arizona Avenue and Foxhall Road.
 Wisconsin Avenue NW between M and K streets.
 K Street NW between 27th Street and Wisconsin Avenue.
 Madison Drive NW between Third and 15th streets.
 Jefferson Drive SW between Third and 15th streets.
 Independence Avenue SW between 23rd and 12th streets.
 D.C. police said they will ticket and tow vehicles parked in violation of posted emergency restrictions.
 RELATED | Running the Marine Corps Marathon? These mistakes could derail your race 
 Street and bridge closures follow early Sunday 
 The streets listed above are scheduled to close to vehicle traffic from approximately 5:30 a.m. to 3 p.m. Sunday .
 Additional closures during that period include:
 Rock Creek Parkway NW between Calvert Street and Ohio Drive.
 14th Street SW between Independence Avenue and the 14th Street Bridge.
 The HOV lanes of the 14th Street Bridge.
 Key Bridge.
 Memorial Bridge.
 Motorists should expect delays and increased pedestrian traffic near the course. Police said all closure times are subject to change.
 Arlington restrictions extend into the afternoon 
 Southbound Route 110 between Washington Boulevard and Route 1 is scheduled to remain closed until 5 p.m. Sunday following its Saturday afternoon closure.
 Other restrictions will affect roads around Rosslyn, the Pentagon and Crystal City, including portions of Route 110, Richmond Highway, Washington Boulevard, Fort Myer Drive, North Lynn Street and Crystal Drive. Several Interstate 395 ramps and express lane access points will also close.
 Reopening times vary by location and depend on race operations and course cleanup. Drivers should consult the Arlington County closure advisory before traveling.
 Metro opens early, but buses will detour 
 Metrorail will open at 5 a.m. Sunday to help runners reach the starting area. Runners can use Pentagon station, while spectators can access viewing locations near Smithsonian, Crystal City and L’Enfant Plaza. Arlington Cemetery station will open at approximately 9 a.m.
 RELATED | Marine Corps Marathon brings early Metro opening and widespread bus detours 
 Bus riders should check their routes before leaving. Marathon detours are scheduled between 2:30 a.m. and 7 p.m. , affecting service around the Pentagon, Rosslyn, Crystal City and parts of D.C. Details are available in Metro’s marathon detour advisory .
 Drivers and transit riders should allow extra travel time and follow posted signs and police directions. Updates will be available through @DCPoliceTraffic , Arlington Alert and Metro’s service alerts.
